## Episode Thesis

This is a macro episode of Inderes' Finnish podcast (inderesPodi 262), with Inderes' economist and its head analyst. They say the global economy is holding up better than expected despite the energy shock from the Iran/Hormuz crisis (IMF: 3.1% growth this year, 3.4% next), and that Germany could become the euro area's growth engine as public investment starts flowing. They also discuss sticky inflation, rising long-term rates (driven by government debt, central banks stepping back from bond markets and AI capex funding) and Inderes raising its risk-free rate in valuation models from 2.5% to 3%. The investor takeaway is that valuations are back to roughly the long-term median P/E of about 14, and that companies with pricing power, competitive moats and light capital needs should pull away from those with weak demand.
